server.name: Manager AI
tool.get_issue_details.description:
Get all details of a specific issue. Returns: id, project_id, name, description, status, priority, specification (markdown), plan (markdown), recap (markdown), tasks (atomic plan tasks), created_at, updated_at.

Issue state machine: NEW → REASONING → PLANNED → ACCEPTED → FINISHED (or CANCELED from any state).
tool.get_issue_status.description:
Get the current status of an issue.

Issue state machine: NEW → REASONING → PLANNED → ACCEPTED → FINISHED (or CANCELED from any state).
tool.get_project_context.description: Get project information (name, path, description, tech_stack).
tool.set_issue_name.description: Set the name of an issue after analysis. Can be called at any point to give the issue a meaningful title.
tool.complete_issue.description:
Mark an issue as Finished and save the recap. Only works for issues in Accepted status. All tasks must be completed first. Call this ONLY when the user explicitly asks you to complete the issue.

This is the final step in the workflow: create_issue_spec → create_issue_plan → create_plan_tasks → (user accepts plan) → (user starts implementation) → (implement & update tasks) → (user asks to complete) → complete_issue.
tool.create_issue.description: Create a new issue in a project. Parameters: project_id (required), description (required, non-empty), priority (optional int 1-5, default 3). Returns the created issue {id, project_id, description, priority, status='New'}. Use this to autonomously file work items. The issue starts in New status — use create_issue_spec next to move it into Reasoning.
tool.create_issue_spec.description:
Write a specification for an issue and move it to Reasoning status. Only works for issues in New status.

This is the first step in the issue workflow. After writing the spec, use create_issue_plan to write the implementation plan.
tool.edit_issue_spec.description: Update the specification of an issue in Reasoning status. Use this to refine the spec before creating a plan.
tool.create_issue_plan.description:
Write an implementation plan for an issue and move it to Planned status. Only works for issues in Reasoning status.

After creating the plan, use create_plan_tasks to define atomic tasks, then the user can accept_issue to begin implementation.
tool.edit_issue_plan.description: Update the implementation plan of an issue in Planned status. Use this to incorporate feedback before the plan is accepted.
tool.accept_issue.description:
Accept an issue's plan and move it to Accepted status. Only works for issues in Planned status. Call this ONLY when the user explicitly asks you to accept the plan.

After acceptance, wait for the user to tell you to begin implementation. Do NOT automatically start implementing — the user controls when work begins.
tool.cancel_issue.description: Cancel an issue from any status. Use this when the issue is no longer needed or was created in error.
tool.create_plan_tasks.description:
Create atomic tasks for an issue's plan. Accepts a list of task objects with 'name' field. Tasks track implementation progress.

Call this after create_issue_plan to break the plan into trackable steps.
tool.force_finish_issue.description: Force finish an issue from any status, bypassing all constraints (status checks, task completion requirements). Use this when an issue needs to be marked as Finished regardless of its current state. Optional recap parameter.
tool.replace_plan_tasks.description: Replace all tasks for an issue. Deletes existing tasks and creates new ones from the provided list. Use this when the plan changes significantly.
tool.update_task_status.description: Update the status of an atomic plan task. Valid transitions: Pending → In Progress → Completed.
tool.update_task_name.description: Update the name of an atomic plan task.
tool.delete_task.description: Delete a single atomic plan task.
tool.get_plan_tasks.description: Get all atomic plan tasks for an issue, ordered by execution order.
tool.send_notification.description:
Send a notification to the user via the Manager AI web interface. Use this to notify the user when:
- You need their input or a decision (e.g., plan is ready for review)
- A significant milestone is reached (e.g., all tasks completed)
- An error or blocker requires their attention

Do NOT use this for routine status updates — update task statuses instead so the user can track progress in the UI.
tool.update_project_context.description: Update the project context (description and/or tech_stack). Only updates fields that are provided.
tool.get_next_issue.description: Get the next workable issue for a project, ordered by priority. Returns an ACCEPTED issue (ready for implementation) first, then a NEW issue (needs planning). Returns null if no workable issues exist. Only call this when the user explicitly asks for the next issue — do NOT use it to automatically chain work.
tool.memory_create.description: Create a memory (title + description, optional parent_id) scoped to a project. Memories are long-term notes the LLM manages across sessions. Use this to record decisions, patterns, constraints, and user preferences.
tool.memory_update.description: Update a memory's title, description, or parent_id. Passing a new parent_id moves the memory; cycles are rejected.
tool.memory_delete.description: Delete a memory. Cascades links; children's parent_id becomes null.
tool.memory_get.description: Fetch a memory with its parent, children, outgoing and incoming links.
tool.memory_list.description: List memories for a project. Optional parent_id filters to one branch (use empty string for root-level memories).
tool.memory_link.description: Create a lateral link between two memories (same project). Optional relation label (e.g. 'see_also', 'contradicts').
tool.memory_unlink.description: Remove a lateral link (matches from_id + to_id + relation).
tool.memory_get_related.description: Get parent, children, and both directions of lateral links for a memory.
tool.memory_search.description: Full-text search across a project's memory titles and descriptions (SQLite FTS5). Returns matches with snippet and rank.
tool.list_project_files.description: List all files uploaded by the user to a project. Returns id, original_name, file_type, file_size, extraction_status (pending/ok/failed/unsupported), low_text flag, created_at. Use this first to discover attached materials (specs, PDFs, spreadsheets) before searching or reading them.
tool.read_project_file.description: Read the extracted text content of an uploaded file. Supports pagination via offset/max_chars (default 50000, hard cap 500000). Returns {id, name, type, status, content, offset, total_chars, truncated, error}. Only files with extraction_status='ok' contain text. Legacy .doc/.xls are 'unsupported' — ask user to re-upload as .docx/.xlsx.
tool.search_project_files.description: Full-text search (SQLite FTS5) across filenames and extracted content of uploaded project files. Returns matches with snippet and rank. Use this when you know keywords but not which file contains them. Pattern: list_project_files → search_project_files → read_project_file.
tool.get_project_url.description: Get the web application URL for a project (for Playwright browser testing). Returns null if project has no URL configured.
tool.list_plugins.description: List all MCP plugins configured for a project.
tool.get_plugin_config.description: Get the full configuration of a specific plugin (no secrets). Returns name, transport, command/url, args, env var names (not values), access_level, timeout.
tool.enable_plugin.description: Enable a plugin and start it. Writes enabled=true to plugins.yaml and spawns the plugin process. Returns success status.
tool.disable_plugin.description: Disable a plugin and stop it. Writes enabled=false to plugins.yaml and terminates the plugin process. Returns success status.
tool.get_project_links.description: Get all directional links for a project (both outgoing and incoming). Each link has source_project_id, target_project_id, source_project_name, target_project_name, and description explaining how they relate. Use this to discover which projects might be impacted by changes.
tool.ask_user_question.description: Ask the user a question through the Manager AI interface. Use this EVERY time you need user input — never use inline text questions or AskUserQuestion. The question appears in the Issue page and the global Questions page. The user can pick an option or write a custom answer. This tool blocks until the user answers or the timeout expires. Parameters: issue_id (required), question (required), options (optional list of strings), timeout_seconds (optional int, default 300).
tool.create_agent.description: Create a new agent. Parameters: name (required), intent (optional string describing what the agent does), model (optional), allowed_tools (optional list of strings), provider (optional string, default 'claude'). Returns the created agent with id, name, intent, model, allowed_tools, provider.
tool.list_agents.description: List all agents. Returns a list of agents with id, name, intent, model, allowed_tools.
tool.get_agent.description: Get a single agent by ID. Returns the agent with id, name, intent, model, allowed_tools.
tool.update_agent.description: Update an existing agent. Parameters: agent_id (required), name (optional), intent (optional), model (optional), allowed_tools (optional), provider (optional). Only provided fields are updated.
tool.delete_agent.description: Delete an agent by ID. Returns {deleted: true} on success.
tool.create_pipeline.description: Create a new pipeline with steps for a project. Parameters: project_id (required), name (required), steps (required list of {agent_id, order_index}). Returns the created pipeline with id, name, and steps.
tool.list_pipelines.description: List all pipelines for a project. Parameters: project_id (required). Returns a list of pipelines with id, name, and steps (each with agent_id, order_index).
tool.get_pipeline.description: Get a single pipeline by ID. Parameters: pipeline_id (required). Returns the pipeline with id, name, steps, and timestamps.
tool.update_pipeline.description: Update a pipeline's name. Parameters: pipeline_id (required), name (required). Returns the updated pipeline.
tool.delete_pipeline.description: Delete a pipeline. Parameters: pipeline_id (required). Returns {deleted: true}.
tool.add_step.description: Add a step to a pipeline. Parameters: pipeline_id (required), agent_id (required), order_index (optional int, auto-assigned if 0). Returns the updated pipeline.
tool.remove_step.description: Remove a step from a pipeline. Parameters: step_id (required). Returns {deleted: true}.
tool.reorder_steps.description: Reorder steps in a pipeline. Parameters: pipeline_id (required), step_ids (required list of step IDs in new order). Returns the pipeline with steps in the new order.
tool.run_pipeline.description: Start a pipeline run for an issue. Parameters: project_id (required), pipeline_id (required), issue_id (required), orchestrated (optional bool, default false). When orchestrated=false (default): runs automatically — spawns Claude for each step sequentially. When orchestrated=true: creates the run in WAITING_FOR_STEP mode — Hermes controls each step manually via start_pipeline_step, advance_pipeline, etc. Returns the created run with id, status, steps, and timing. Only one run per issue at a time.
tool.get_pipeline_run_status.description: Get the status of a pipeline run. Parameters: run_id (required). Returns run details with id, status, current_step_index, and each step's agent_name, status, and timing.
tool.send_agent_message.description: Send a message from an agent within a pipeline run. Parameters: run_id (required), sender_agent_name (required), content (required). Returns the created message with id, sender, content, and timestamp.
tool.get_pipeline_messages.description: Get all messages for a pipeline run, ordered by creation time. Parameters: run_id (required). Returns a list of messages with id, sender_agent_name, content, and created_at.
tool.get_active_pipeline_run.description: Get the currently active (RUNNING) pipeline run for an issue. Parameters: issue_id (required). Returns: run_id, pipeline_id, status, current_step_index, and all step details including agent names, statuses, and terminal_ids. Returns null if no pipeline is running for this issue.
tool.get_active_agent.description: Returns YOUR identity as the active pipeline agent. You ARE this agent — the returned agent_name and agent_intent describe YOU and what you must do. Parameters: issue_id (required). Returns: run_id, step_run_id, agent_name, agent_intent, step_index, step_status, terminal_id. Returns {active: null} if no pipeline is running or no step is active. This is the ONLY source of agent identity — there are no env vars.
tool.finished_pipeline_step.description: Signal completion of your pipeline step. Call this when you have finished all work for your step. Parameters: issue_id (required), summary (required, string — handoff summary for the next agent). Returns: {success, step_completed, pipeline_finished}. The pipeline automatically advances to the next step. When rejected=True and target_step_index is omitted, the system checks pipeline event rules for auto-resolve.
tool.add_pipeline_event_rule.description: Add an event rule to a pipeline. Parameters: pipeline_id (required), event_type (required, one of: step_completed, step_rejected, step_failed, pipeline_completed), source_step_id (required), target_step_id (required), action_type (optional, default 'redirect', or 'set_issue_status', 'emit_event'), action_params (optional, dict). For action_type='set_issue_status', pass action_params={"status": "PLANNED"}. For action_type='emit_event', pass action_params={"event_type": "my_event", ...}. Returns the created rule.
tool.remove_pipeline_event_rule.descript: Delete an event rule by ID. Returns {deleted: true}.
tool.list_pipeline_event_rules.descripti: List all event rules for a pipeline. Parameters: pipeline_id (required). Returns list of rules.
tool.update_pipeline_event_rule.descript: Update specific fields on a pipeline event rule. Only provided fields are changed. Parameters: rule_id (required), event_type (optional), source_step_id (optional), target_step_id (optional), action_type (optional), action_params (optional, dict), enabled (optional, bool). Returns the updated rule.
tool.start_pipeline_step.description: Avvia lo step corrente di una pipeline orchestrata. Chiamato da Hermes. Spawna Claude Code in un terminale PTY visibile nell'interfaccia di Manager AI. La pipeline DEVE essere in stato WAITING_FOR_STEP. Parametri: run_id (required), project_id (required). Restituisce term_id, agent_name, agent_intent, step_index, step_run_id.
tool.advance_pipeline.description: Avanza la pipeline orchestrata al prossimo step. Chiamato da Hermes DOPO aver analizzato i risultati dello step completato. La pipeline deve essere in stato WAITING_FOR_STEP e lo step corrente deve essere COMPLETED. Se era l'ultimo step, la pipeline viene segnata come COMPLETED. Parametri: run_id (required). Restituisce: status, next_step_index, pipeline_finished.
tool.pause_pipeline.description: Mette in pausa la pipeline orchestrata o non orchestrata. Se uno step è in esecuzione (RUNNING), il terminale viene killato e lo step marcato FAILED. La pipeline può essere ripresa con resume_pipeline. Parametri: run_id (required).
tool.resume_pipeline.description: Riprende una pipeline in pausa (PAUSED). La rimette in stato WAITING_FOR_STEP, pronta per start_pipeline_step. Parametri: run_id (required).
